name: Jane Street
research: Market maker headquartered in New York with a large London desk. Hires generalist quantitative traders and researchers straight from degree programmes and trains them internally; no finance background expected. Interview is famously heavy on probability, mental arithmetic and estimation under pressure. Best hook: a concrete estimation or trading puzzle you worked through, or a view on market-making in an asset class they touch.

name: Optiver
research: Amsterdam-headquartered market maker with offices in London, Chicago, Sydney, Shanghai, Taipei, Mumbai and Austin. Structured graduate pipeline: weeks of classroom training then placement on a desk. Strong internal teaching culture, so they reward people who learn fast and explain clearly. Best hook: something specific about market-making mechanics or a trading game you built.

name: IMC Trading
research: Amsterdam market maker with a real London presence, trading options, futures, equities and bonds. Smaller and more boutique than Optiver or Jane Street, with the same graduate training model. Best hook: a specific product or asset class, and evidence you have thought about liquidity provision rather than directional bets.

name: Flow Traders
research: Amsterdam-listed ETP market maker that opened a Paris trading hub, which makes it one of the few market makers recruiting directly in Paris. Covers ETFs, fixed income and FX. Best hook: the Paris build-out itself, or the mechanics of ETF creation and redemption.

name: Citadel Securities
research: Market maker, separate business from Citadel the hedge fund, with a very large London operation. Hires quantitative researchers, traders and software engineers. Extremely competitive and well paid. Best hook: a technical edge - latency, execution, or a model - stated concretely.

name: XTX Markets
research: London-based, machine-learning-driven market maker, deliberately flat and highly technical with a small headcount. Known for paying at the very top of the market and for being highly selective. Hires mathematicians and ML people more than finance people. Best hook: a research result or model, not a career story.

name: Qube Research and Technologies
research: Systematic fund founded in London, now one of the heaviest quant employers in the city, across research, data and engineering. Combines a research culture with serious technology. Best hook: a signal, dataset or backtesting approach - they respond to method, not enthusiasm.

name: G-Research
research: Systematic machine-learning fund with London and Paris offices, closely tied to the systematic trading community and a visible sponsor of quant conferences and events. Heavy Python and ML stack. Best hook: a specific ML approach applied to financial data, or something from their public research.

name: Squarepoint Capital
research: Systematic fund with large London and New York operations and one of the highest quant hiring volumes in London. Research and engineering sit close together. Best hook: a concrete research idea and your implementation of it.

name: Balyasny Asset Management
research: Chicago multi-strategy fund that has expanded hard in London and Paris. Pod model: individual portfolio managers control their own hiring budget, which makes contacting a PM directly far more effective here than at a bank. Best hook: fit to a specific pod's strategy.

name: Millennium Management
research: New York multi-strategy fund, same pod model as Balyasny, hiring continuously across teams. No central graduate funnel - hiring is entirely at pod level. Best hook: a specific team's strategy and what you would bring to it. Cold outreach to PMs genuinely works here.

name: Point72 Asset Management
research: Stamford-based multi-strategy fund with a structured Academy programme for juniors plus a systematic arm. London office is substantial. Best hook: the Academy if you are early career, otherwise a specific strategy team.

name: Schonfeld Strategic Advisors
research: New York multi-strategy fund with a strong and growing London presence across systematic and discretionary teams. Mid-sized, less brand-saturated than Millennium or Citadel, so outreach stands out more. Best hook: a specific desk and a concrete skill match.

name: ExodusPoint Capital Management
research: Large multi-strategy fund with a big London quant and engineering footprint. Tech-heavy and quantitative in culture. Best hook: technical contribution - research pipeline, data infrastructure, or model work.

name: CFM
research: Capital Fund Management, the flagship Paris systematic hedge fund, founded by physicist Jean-Philippe Bouchaud. Academic culture, publishes research openly, hires from maths and physics. The obvious first call for anyone who wants to stay in Paris and do genuine quant research. Best hook: one of their published papers, named specifically - they will notice that you actually read it.

name: Syquant Capital
research: Small Paris systematic fund. Fewer than a hundred people, so contacting a portfolio manager directly is realistic and often productive. Best hook: something specific about their strategy, plus willingness to do the unglamorous work.

name: BNP Paribas
research: French universal bank with a large global markets division covering quant, strats and structuring across Paris and London. Runs structured graduate programmes in corporate and institutional banking. Best hook: a specific asset class desk and the graduate intake timing.

name: Societe Generale
research: French bank whose equity derivatives and structuring franchise is among the strongest in Europe, with quant teams split between Paris and London. Large graduate intake. Best hook: a product or structuring idea, or the Paris-London split of their teams.

name: Credit Agricole CIB
research: French corporate and investment bank with strong rates and credit quant teams in Paris and London. Smaller markets headcount than BNP or SocGen, which usually means more direct access to desk heads. Best hook: rates or credit specifics.

name: Deutsche Bank
research: German bank whose London operation is one of the largest quant and structuring hubs in Europe. Large and well-structured graduate intake with defined timelines. Best hook: the specific desk and programme, plus a technical artefact.

name: Barclays
research: UK universal bank with a big London markets floor, quantitative analytics teams and a structured sales and trading graduate programme. Best hook: a specific desk within global markets and the graduate cycle.

name: Marshall Wace
research: London hedge fund combining a large systematic equity platform with fundamental long-short. Hires both quants and fundamental analysts. Best hook: their systematic alpha capture approach, or a specific industry view.

name: Man Group
research: London-listed alternative asset manager running AHL (systematic futures), Man Numeric and GLG. One of the few large systematic managers with genuinely structured graduate intake. Best hook: AHL's trend-following heritage or a systematic factor idea.

name: Brevan Howard
research: London macro hedge fund with a reputation for rigour and small, senior teams. Hiring is selective and relationship-driven rather than volume-driven. Best hook: a macro view, stated with actual reasoning behind it.

name: Rokos Capital Management
research: London macro fund founded by Chris Rokos, systematic-leaning, small team, highly selective. Best hook: a macro or rates research idea. Only worth contacting if you can say something genuinely substantive.

name: Eisler Capital
research: London multi-strategy fund that has grown quickly since launch. Still small enough that direct approaches to desk leads work. Best hook: specific strategy fit and speed of contribution.

name: Walleye Capital
research: Systematic and volatility trading firm with London presence. Mid-sized, less saturated than the largest multi-strategies. Best hook: volatility or options research.

name: Verition Fund Management
research: Greenwich multi-strategy fund with a real London operation. Pod structure, so team-level outreach works. Best hook: a specific team and a matching skill.

name: Maven Securities
research: London systematic options trading firm, small and highly technical. Hires in low numbers and cares deeply about options intuition. Best hook: an options or volatility surface question answered properly.

name: Amundi
research: Largest European asset manager, headquartered in Paris, with quantitative research, index and multi-asset teams. Structured graduate programmes and a large intake, making it one of the few realistic Paris routes at scale. Best hook: a specific quant team, factor research, or their systematic range.

name: Tobam
research: Paris systematic asset manager known for its anti-benchmark and diversification-weighted approach, with a distinctly research-led culture and a small team. Best hook: their published methodology - read it and have an actual opinion.

name: Ossiam
research: Paris systematic and ETF asset manager, part of Natixis, with a quant research culture and a smaller team than the big houses. Best hook: a specific systematic strategy in their range and a concrete question about it.

name: AQR Capital Management
research: Systematic asset manager founded in 1998 out of Goldman Sachs Asset Management by Cliff Asness and colleagues. Runs factor-based strategies (value, momentum, carry, defensive) across equities, macro and alternatives, and publishes its research openly, which is unusual for the industry. Academic in tone: PhDs in finance, economics, maths and physics are the norm. Best hook: a factor research idea or a specific AQR paper you have actually tested, not just read.

name: AXA Investment Managers
research: Paris-based asset manager owned by the AXA insurance group, with quantitative research, multi-asset and structured product teams. A realistic Paris route with a real graduate intake. Note the entity is in flux - AXA IM and BNP Paribas Asset Management announced plans to combine, so check the current status before you name a team in an email. Best hook: a specific quant or multi-asset team, and evidence you know the ownership situation is changing.

name: Bank of America
research: US universal bank whose markets arm, BofA Securities, runs quant and strats teams across rates, credit, FX and equities. London is the main European hub; Paris coverage runs through BofA Securities Europe. Structured analyst and summer programmes with fixed application windows, so timing matters more here than at a hedge fund. Best hook: a named desk plus the specific programme and its deadline.

name: BlackRock
research: The largest asset manager in the world. Two distinct doors for a quant: the systematic investing arm (factor and signal-driven equity and fixed income) and Aladdin, their risk and portfolio platform, which is closer to a technology firm than an asset manager. London is one of their largest offices. Best hook: Aladdin, or a systematic research idea - and be specific about which of the two you want, because they hire very differently.

name: Bridgewater Associates
research: The largest hedge fund in the world, founded by Ray Dalio, running systematic macro through Pure Alpha and All Weather. Culture is the differentiator and the filter: radical transparency, recorded meetings, written principles, and a famously demanding interview process. They want people who can reason from first principles about economies, not people who know finance. Best hook: a macro or systematic view you can actually defend, plus genuine comfort with their culture - do not fake that part.

name: Citadel
research: Multi-strategy hedge fund founded by Ken Griffin, separate from Citadel Securities. Operates as sector and strategy teams with significant autonomy, and hires continuously rather than through a single graduate funnel. London is a substantial office. Extremely competitive and pays accordingly. Best hook: a specific strategy team and concrete technical depth - a generic application to 'Citadel' goes nowhere.

name: Citigroup
research: US universal bank with a large markets and securities services franchise. Quant and strats work sits across rates, FX, credit and equity derivatives. London is the biggest European hub, with a Paris presence. Runs structured analyst programmes with fixed windows. Best hook: a named desk and the programme you are targeting, plus something concrete you have built for that asset class.

name: D. E. Shaw and Co
research: New York quantitative hedge fund founded in 1988 by David Shaw, and one of the most secretive firms in the industry. Hires almost entirely from computer science, maths and physics, with a technology culture closer to a research lab than a fund. London office. They rarely advertise specific roles, so a strong direct approach is often the only route. Best hook: a technical or research artefact with measurable results - they respond to evidence of ability, not to interest in finance.

name: DRW
research: Chicago-based proprietary trading firm founded by Don Wilson, active across futures, options, fixed income and crypto through Cumberland. Engineering-led and considerably less brand-saturated than the big market makers, which means a direct email stands out more. London office. Best hook: a market structure or trading idea, or a systems project - and the fact that you contacted a person rather than a portal.

name: Goldman Sachs
research: US investment bank, and the firm that gave the industry the strats model - quantitative people embedded on trading desks rather than in a separate research silo. Global markets covers quant, strats and structuring across rates, credit, FX and equities. London is the largest European hub, with Paris coverage. Best hook: the strats organisation specifically, or a named desk - 'quantitative finance at Goldman Sachs' is too vague to action.

name: Hudson River Trading
research: Algorithmic trading firm headquartered in New York with a large London office, known for being engineering-first: C++, low latency, hardware, and a research culture that treats trading as a systems problem. Trades across most liquid asset classes. Hires strong engineers and quantitative researchers, not finance specialists. Best hook: a low-latency systems project or a research result with real numbers behind it.

name: J.P. Morgan
research: The largest US bank, with a global markets division spanning quant, strats and structuring, and a quantitative research group whose published work is read across the industry. London is a major hub; Paris is present. Large structured graduate and analyst intake with fixed deadlines. Best hook: their own published quant research, or a named desk - referencing a specific paper is a strong signal here because so few applicants do it.

name: Jump Trading
research: Chicago-headquartered high-frequency trading firm founded by Bill DiSomma and Paul Gurinas, deliberately low profile and engineering-driven, with a significant crypto arm in Jump Crypto. Trades futures, equities, options and digital assets. London office. Best hook: something low-level and technical - a performance engineering result, a custom data structure, anything where you can point at a number.

name: Morgan Stanley
research: US investment bank with a particularly strong equity derivatives and structuring franchise, plus quant and strats teams across rates, credit and FX. London is a major European hub and Paris is present. Runs a large, structured analyst programme with a fixed application window. Best hook: equity derivatives or structuring specifically, and a product or pricing idea rather than a general expression of interest.

name: Renaissance Technologies
research: The most successful quantitative fund in history, founded by Jim Simons and running the Medallion fund from Long Island. Famously secretive, hires almost exclusively scientists - maths, physics, computer science, statistics - and has very low staff turnover, which means openings are rare and competition is extreme. Be realistic about the odds, but do not self-select out. Best hook: exceptional scientific or mathematical credentials, stated plainly and without embellishment.

name: Susquehanna International Group
research: Philadelphia-based options market maker founded by Jeff Yass, with a strong culture of decision-making under uncertainty - they famously train new traders using poker and game theory. European headquarters in Dublin, plus a London office. Trades options, ETFs and equities. Best hook: probability and expected-value reasoning, and genuine evidence that you think in bets rather than in certainties.

name: Tower Research Capital
research: New York-headquartered high-frequency trading firm founded by Mark Gorton, operating low-latency strategies globally across futures, equities and FX. Engineering and infrastructure heavy, with a London office. Less visible than the best-known HFT names, so a targeted email is more likely to be read. Best hook: a latency, networking or systems engineering project with concrete performance numbers.

name: Two Sigma
research: New York quantitative hedge fund founded by John Overdeck and David Siegel, systematic across asset classes with a heavy emphasis on data, machine learning and engineering. London office. Unusually for a fund, they run structured internship and new-graduate programmes, which makes them more reachable for a junior than most of their peers. Best hook: a data science or machine learning project applied to real, messy data - and be specific about the pipeline, not just the model.

name: UBS
research: Swiss bank that absorbed Credit Suisse, making it the dominant Swiss player and one of the largest markets businesses in Europe. Global markets covers quant, strats and structuring across rates, credit, FX and equities. London is a major hub with a Paris presence. The integration means disruption but also genuine hiring need. Best hook: a specific desk plus awareness of the integration - naming it shows you follow the firm rather than a generic list.

name: Mistral AI
research: Paris frontier lab shipping open-weight models; applied-science and research-engineering hires out of the same pool. Best hook: name the open-weight, French-sovereign angle and one model you actually ran.

name: Hugging Face
research: Runs the open model hub with a large Paris office; platform and applied-research teams rather than a pure services arm. Best hook: a concrete contribution or model card you read closely, not the hub's size.

name: Dataiku
research: Paris-born enterprise data science platform; substantial solutions-AI engineering bench alongside the core product. Best hook: a production data product you shipped end to end, and the stakeholders it served.

name: Ekimetrics
research: Data science consultancy turned AI partner for luxury, CPG and finance; modelling work is client-facing. Best hook: a client problem where modelling had to survive contact with the business, not the model itself.

name: Artefact
research: Data and AI consulting with a real engineering bench in Paris and London, not only advisory decks. Best hook: a project where the engineering mattered as much as the model, said concretely.

name: Sia Partners
research: Paris consulting group with a dedicated AI and data practice that hires and builds rather than only staffing. Best hook: an AI use case you scoped with a non-technical stakeholder and got adopted.

name: Google DeepMind
research: London research lab with applied product teams; scientist and research-engineer tracks are separate but adjacent. Best hook: a paper or method you can argue about, and where you would take it next.

name: Faculty AI
research: London applied-AI company shipping production ML for public and private sector clients. Best hook: applied ML that shipped, and how you would have measured it.

name: Quantexa
research: Decision-intelligence platform used heavily in financial crime; data science and ML engineering both hiring. Best hook: entity resolution or graph reasoning at scale, framed as a real detection problem.
